quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle, you should check all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals. Paint damage does not affect safe riding.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding next to a car?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only dangerous on wet roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to a car is dangerous because the driver may not see you. The car will also block your escape path.

questions.question: What type of shoes should you wear when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels short so they don't catch on anything. Tuck in laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Why is clothing important when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: It should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
It should leave your arms or legs uncovered.
You should skip a jacket in warm weather.
It can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you during a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly but not restrict your movement.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you prepare for?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
Other drivers seeing you and staying away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull out. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space from hazards.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car, what happens?

options.text: You are most visible to the driver.
The driver may not see you without using the side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you without using the side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver sees you in the rearview mirror. Drivers check the rearview mirror much more than the side mirror. This position helps them see you.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Don't use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible. Use your headlight at all times, including during the day.

questions.question: What does space between your motorcycle and other vehicles do?

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you stuck in one area of the lane.
Lets you rely on others to spot dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle helps you react and respond if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face as well as a face shield.
Your face the same as a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your face. A face shield provides full face protection and is better. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not use your rearview mirrors to watch traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to move if the vehicle backs up or if another vehicle comes up too fast from behind.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other vehicles and makes it easier for them to see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should stop other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Lets the rider use engine braking.
Should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the rider use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting smoothly is helpful for riders. If you use engine braking, press your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you drink one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding skills can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on your body.
There is an effect, but it only lasts a short time.
There is an effect, but coffee can remove it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding skills can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can harm the skills you need for safe riding. Your body needs time to eliminate alcohol—coffee cannot speed this up.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle you do not know, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to check if it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you normally do since most bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is a bit different, so be careful with an unfamiliar one. Learn how it works before you ride. Practice the gear pattern by working the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment:

options.text: Starts at about half the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Starts with the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can harm your riding skills. You can be impaired well below the legal alcohol limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because turn signals cannot be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle. Learn where all controls are located before you ride.

questions.question: Is riding at night usually easier or harder?

options.text: Easier, because you can see the lights of other vehicles more clearly.
Harder, because you cannot see as well.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder, because you cannot see as well.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is reduced. It is more difficult to see other vehicles and judge distances without natural light.

questions.question: Which organization certifies helmets for maximum protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: U.S. Department of Transportation
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet certified by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) for the best protection.

questions.question: How can you make yourself more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright or reflective clothing. You can also add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed.

questions.question: What should you watch for when passing parked cars?

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space
Cars pulling out of parking spaces

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be careful. Vehicles may pull away from the curb or exit parking spaces without warning.
